open_points.subject: owner authentication and private disclosure channel
open_points.text: “Reaches the kernel through the agent channel with the owner's token” and “the owner alone reads [personal data]” do not say how an owner-token response traverses an agent channel without the agent reading it.
open_points.question: What trusted component authenticates the owner and displays owner-only values or approval requests without exposing them to the agent operating the channel?
options: The MCP client has a separate owner-only UI and credential path
The language-model agent relays owner requests and responses
Owner-only values are returned through a second protected channel
open_points.default_guess: Require a separate owner-authenticated UI path within the MCP client that the agent cannot observe.

open_points.subject: owner credential lifecycle
open_points.text: “the owner's token” is named, but only agent tokens are described as configured, reloaded and revoked.
open_points.question: Where is the owner token provisioned, how is it verified and rotated or revoked, and what happens when it is absent or invalid?
options: One protected installation token with an operational rotation procedure
A host-proxy identity mapped to the owner
A persistent owner credential managed by the kernel
open_points.default_guess: Use one protected installation token, verified in constant time and rotated operationally.

open_points.subject: proxy-to-kernel boundary
open_points.text: “one inbound channel, `mcp`, behind the host's reverse proxy” assigns brute-force protection to the proxy but does not state whether the kernel trusts proxy identity, accepts only local traffic, or authenticates every request itself.
open_points.question: What security property must the reverse-proxy boundary provide, and where are owner and agent tokens authenticated?
options: The kernel authenticates every MCP request and trusts the proxy only for rate limiting
The proxy authenticates callers and passes a trusted identity
Both layers authenticate
open_points.default_guess: Have the kernel authenticate every request and use the proxy only for transport termination and rate limiting.

open_points.subject: platform manifest authority
open_points.text: “Microservices — known only as records of the platform manifest” does not name who supplies or changes the manifest, how the kernel obtains it, or whether its contents are trusted.
open_points.question: Who owns the manifest, how does the kernel load and refresh it, and which manifest fields are trusted versus validated?
options: Protected installation configuration loaded on change
A signed manifest fetched from a platform service
A kernel-managed manifest changed through an owner action
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as protected installation configuration loaded atomically when changed.

open_points.subject: microservice transport identity
open_points.text: “the kernel calls microservices over their HTTP APIs” and “service credentials ... live in ... protected configuration” do not define how an endpoint is authenticated or what transport is required.
open_points.question: How does the kernel authenticate a selected service instance and protect requests and responses in transit?
options: HTTPS with certificate validation plus configured service credentials
A trusted private network with plain HTTP
Per-service transport rules declared by the manifest
open_points.default_guess: Require HTTPS certificate validation and configured per-service credentials.

open_points.subject: secret-echo withholding
open_points.text: “A service's own answer that echoes one verbatim is withheld” does not say what replaces the value, whether the node or run fails, or whether the owner may receive it.
open_points.question: What observable node, run and trace result is produced when a response contains a configured secret verbatim?
options: Fail the node with a secret-disclosure refusal and store no response payload
Return a digest-and-class placeholder
Withhold it only from agents but return it to the owner
open_points.default_guess: Fail the node with a distinct secret-disclosure reason and retain only safe metadata.

open_points.subject: submission of outside material
open_points.text: “until the owner or an agent submits it” names a submission that is absent from the primary actions and does not identify what is submitted.
open_points.question: Which kernel action submits outside material, and is its input an intake-record reference, ordinary value, or file?
options: The normal run action supplies an intake-record reference
A separate submit action imports an intake record
An operation node reads the service intake without any kernel submission
open_points.default_guess: Treat an intake-record reference as a normal value supplied when starting a run.

open_points.subject: inspection request and result
open_points.text: “inspect functions, flows, runs, bindings, approvals, standing grants and effect attempts” gives only “typed description” and “unknown reference” without saying how collections, individual versions or personal values are selected.
open_points.question: What inputs and result shapes does inspection support, including listing, version selection, filtering and bounded pagination?
options: Separate typed list and get requests for every record kind
One tagged inspect request with list/get variants
Only lookup by exact reference
open_points.default_guess: Use one tagged request with bounded list and exact-get variants for each record kind.

open_points.subject: contract version creation
open_points.text: “the first contract of a new slot name creates the slot” does not say how a later contract version is created, identified, or related to the slot's current contract version.
open_points.question: What input creates a new immutable contract version, and when does it become the slot's current contract version?
options: Authoring new content under the slot automatically makes a new current version
Creation and selection of the current contract are separate actions
A slot can have only one contract version
open_points.default_guess: Create a new immutable version under the slot and make it current atomically.

open_points.subject: content equality and identities
open_points.text: “an existing one when the content is equal” is used for contracts and trial cases, but canonical content and the identity rule are not defined.
open_points.question: How are contract and trial-case contents canonicalized and compared, and what digest or identifier is returned?
options: Canonical serialized form hashed by the kernel
Structural equality after schema-aware normalization
Byte equality of the submitted representation
open_points.default_guess: Use a specified canonical serialization and a cryptographic digest.

open_points.subject: trial-case oracle
open_points.text: “add a trial case” says values fit the ports, while “trial evidence per case” and “every later implementation must pass” never define whether a case contains expected outputs, expected failure, or only inputs.
open_points.question: What fields constitute a trial case and exactly what result makes an implementation pass it?
options: Inputs plus exact expected outputs
Inputs plus output predicates or expected failure
Inputs only, with success meaning termination and contract-valid output
open_points.default_guess: Use inputs plus exact expected outputs, including file fixtures by digest.

open_points.subject: try, submit, admit and activate sequence
open_points.text: “try an implementation” is a separate action, but “admit and activate — kernel, when an implementation is submitted” does not define what submission is or whether authoring, trying and admission are one transaction.
open_points.question: Which request submits an implementation for admission, may a non-authoring agent trigger it, and is activation part of that same request?
options: Author implementation submits it and automatically runs admission and activation
Try submits an already-authored implementation for admission
A distinct submit/admit request is missing
open_points.default_guess: Have authoring store the implementation and atomically run whole-corpus admission, activating it only on success.

open_points.subject: capture of a failed execution
open_points.text: “capture a failed execution into the trial corpus” does not say which node executions are eligible or how a failed execution yields the expected result that later implementations must pass.
open_points.question: Can only failed function-node attempts be captured, and what oracle is stored for the resulting trial case?
options: Capture its input only and require future execution to succeed with any contract-valid output
The caller must supply the corrected expected output
Capture an earlier known-good output for the same input
open_points.default_guess: Limit capture to function-node failures and require the authorized caller to supply an expected output.

open_points.subject: binding proposal identity and replacement
open_points.text: “propose an operation binding” returns “proposed binding” but does not define its name or identity, equality behavior, or whether multiple proposed or accepted bindings may target the same manifest operation.
open_points.question: How are bindings identified and versioned, and what happens when another binding is proposed for an operation that already has one?
options: Named immutable binding versions; multiple bindings may target one operation
Exactly one binding per manifest operation, replaced by a new proposal
Content-addressed bindings without names
open_points.default_guess: Use named immutable binding versions and allow multiple bindings when their typed interfaces differ.

open_points.subject: flow external interface
open_points.text: “compose and prove a flow” describes its graph and proof result but never defines how the flow's own value input and output ports are declared.
open_points.question: How are a flow version's external value inputs and outputs named, typed, classified and connected to graph nodes?
options: Explicit flow input and output port declarations
Unconnected node ports are inferred as the flow interface
Flows have inputs only and return all terminal-node outputs
open_points.default_guess: Require explicit named, schema-typed and disclosure-classed flow input and output ports.

open_points.subject: run inputs and input refusal
open_points.text: “run a flow” does not name the supplied value inputs, their validation, or the failure when they are absent, extra, schema-invalid or over-classified.
open_points.question: What exact input starts a run and what observable refusal is returned for each invalid flow-input condition?
options: A named value map validated before run creation
Inputs are obtained only from source operation nodes
Positional values matching declared flow ports
open_points.default_guess: Accept a named value map, validate it completely before creating a run, and refuse invalid input with reasons.

open_points.subject: effect-decision outcomes
open_points.text: “the effect runs on the exact input shown” conflicts with the settled case where an approved send can encounter an unreachable service and remain approved, and it omits success, service failure and unknown-outcome results.
open_points.question: What result does approve return for sent-and-applied, unreachable-before-send, known service refusal and outcome-unknown cases?
options: A typed effect-attempt state for each outcome
Only the updated run state
Approval returns immediately and all outcomes are learned through inspection
open_points.default_guess: Return the immutable effect attempt plus the updated run state.

open_points.subject: standing-grant eligibility
open_points.text: The action permits a grant for “a node of a flow's active version” except `destructive`, while K-08 says only `state-transition`, `external-effect` and `destructive` ask and that `destructive` never takes a grant.
open_points.question: Must grants be refused for `read` and `draft-write` nodes as well as for `destructive` nodes?
options: Only `state-transition` and `external-effect` nodes are grantable
Every non-destructive operation node is grantable even if it normally does not ask
Read and draft-write grants are accepted but have no effect
open_points.default_guess: Allow grants only for `state-transition` and `external-effect` nodes.

open_points.subject: standing-grant lifecycle after activation changes
open_points.text: A grant belongs to “a node of a flow's active version,” but the texts do not say whether it remains active, becomes inactive, or is automatically revoked when another version is activated.
open_points.question: What happens to grants for the formerly active flow version after activation changes, and can the owner still revoke them?
options: They automatically become inactive but remain inspectable
They remain active for old pinned runs only
Activation is refused until grants are explicitly revoked
open_points.default_guess: Make them inactive for new sends, retain them for audit, and allow explicit revocation.

open_points.subject: read-trace failure
open_points.text: The table claims every action names its failure, but “read a trace” has failure “—”.
open_points.question: What happens for an unknown trace or run reference, an invalid query, or a caller not entitled to the requested value?
options: Typed refusal with a reason
Empty result for unknown references
Inspection-style `unknown reference` failure
open_points.default_guess: Return a typed `unknown_reference` or `invalid_request` refusal and apply disclosure redaction.

open_points.subject: sandbox isolation contract
open_points.text: “disposable isolated environment with bounded time, memory, output and processes” leaves the isolation mechanism and enforceable boundary unnamed.
open_points.question: What sandbox boundary must implementations rely on for Python execution, including process isolation, syscall access, environment variables, filesystem mounts and resource enforcement?
options: A specified container profile
A specified OS sandbox profile
A language-level restricted interpreter
open_points.default_guess: Use a disposable OS-level sandbox with no network, an allowlisted read-only runtime and hard cgroup-style limits.

open_points.subject: function file input and output
open_points.text: K-02 allows “no filesystem beyond its input,” while K-06 describes functions that “produce two kinds of file” and K-10 discusses failed function executions with file inputs.
open_points.question: How does Python code read file inputs and create file outputs without filesystem access beyond its input?
options: Mounted read-only input files plus a bounded writable output directory
Files are passed and returned as byte values through standard I/O
Function nodes may consume but may not produce files
open_points.default_guess: Mount inputs read-only and provide a separate bounded writable output directory whose declared files become outputs.

open_points.subject: deterministic admission environment
open_points.text: “Admission is a deterministic verdict” does not pin the Python/runtime version, platform, locale, hash seed, resource-limit interpretation or case order that can change a verdict.
open_points.question: Which execution-environment facts are pinned into admission evidence so the same implementation and corpus produce the same verdict?
options: Pin a versioned sandbox image and deterministic runtime settings
Treat only logical output comparison as deterministic and allow resource verdicts to vary
Record the current host environment without pinning it
open_points.default_guess: Pin a versioned sandbox image, runtime settings and corpus order in the verdict.

open_points.subject: schema language and equality
open_points.text: “Every port carries a value schema” and “the same schema” do not identify the schema language, supported subset, reference handling or canonical equality rule.
open_points.question: What schema representation is permitted and when are two schemas considered the same?
options: A specified JSON Schema subset with canonical structural equality
Kernel-defined primitive and record types with nominal identifiers
Digest equality of canonical schema documents
open_points.default_guess: Define a closed kernel schema language and compare canonical schema digests.

open_points.subject: map semantics
open_points.text: “a map of a node over a collection” does not define collection ordering, result shape, item failure behavior, concurrency or how approvals work for mapped effect nodes.
open_points.question: What are the deterministic execution and approval semantics of a map, especially when the mapped node is effectful?
options: Sequential ordered items, one trace and approval per item, fail only dependent items
Parallel items with nondeterministic completion order
Map is restricted to function nodes
open_points.default_guess: Preserve input order, execute deterministically, create an attempt and any required approval per item, and return an aligned result collection.

open_points.subject: guard semantics
open_points.text: “a guard on a declared closed value” does not define the value source, branch selection, unmatched-value behavior, output joining or traces for skipped nodes.
open_points.question: How are guard cases declared and proven, and what happens when a value has no matching branch?
options: Exhaustive branches over a closed enum, with skipped-node trace statuses
A required default branch
Unmatched values fail the run
open_points.default_guess: Require exhaustive branches over the schema's closed values and record nonselected nodes as skipped.

open_points.subject: independent-node scheduling
open_points.text: The flow is an acyclic graph, but no rule orders simultaneously ready nodes or effect attempts.
open_points.question: Are ready nodes executed serially in a deterministic order or concurrently, and what order is observable for independent effects and traces?
options: Deterministic serial topological order
Concurrent execution with ordering explicitly unspecified
Concurrency only for pure function nodes
open_points.default_guess: Use a deterministic serial topological order in this one-process kernel.

open_points.subject: effect-class authority
open_points.text: “Authority lives on operation nodes” names the effect classes but does not say whether the manifest, accepted binding, or agent-authored flow assigns the class.
open_points.question: Which trusted record declares an operation's effect class, and how does proof prevent an agent from presenting a write as `read` or `draft-write`?
options: The platform manifest declares it and the binding pins it
The owner assigns it when accepting a binding
The agent assigns it on each operation node
open_points.default_guess: Require the manifest operation record to declare it and include it in the binding's pinned digest.

open_points.subject: idempotency declaration and key
open_points.text: “The kernel supplies the declared idempotency key” does not say where support is declared, how the key is generated and scoped, or where it is inserted into the request.
open_points.question: Which manifest or binding fields define idempotency, and is the key stable per node execution, map item, approval, resend or effect attempt?
options: Manifest-declared header or body location with one stable key per logical effect
Binding-declared key mapping with a new key per send
A fixed HTTP header supported by every effect operation
open_points.default_guess: Pin a manifest-declared request location and generate one stable key per logical node effect, retained across uncertain-outcome resolution and authorized resend.

open_points.subject: HTTP outcome classification
open_points.text: “service is unreachable” and “cannot tell whether an effect happened” do not define how connection failure, timeout, disconnect, HTTP status or invalid response maps to `failed`, unreachable `pending`, or `outcome_unknown`.
open_points.question: What transport observations distinguish definitely-not-sent, known application failure, known success and unknown outcome for reads and effects?
options: A complete phase-based transport outcome table
Treat every transport error on an effect as unknown
Let each binding declare response and failure mapping
open_points.default_guess: Define a phase-based table: failure before any bytes are sent is unreachable, ambiguity after sending is outcome unknown, and declared responses determine known success or failure.

open_points.subject: trace cardinality across attempts
open_points.text: “Every node execution writes one immutable trace record” does not say whether resume, resend and mapped items create new execution records or update one node record.
open_points.question: What is the identity and relationship of node execution, attempt and effect-attempt records across retries, resumes and map items?
options: One immutable execution record per attempt linked to a logical node instance
One node record with a list of immutable attempts
Exactly one record per graph node per run
open_points.default_guess: Create one logical node-instance record and separate immutable attempt records for each execution or send.

open_points.subject: aggregate run completion
open_points.text: “A failed node stops only its dependants” does not say whether independent branches continue or how their mixed outcomes determine the final run status and outputs.
open_points.question: When one branch fails, which other nodes still run, when does the run finish, and is any node failure sufficient for final `failed`?
options: Continue independent branches; finish `failed` after all runnable branches settle
Stop the whole run on the first failure
Continue and report partial success as `succeeded`
open_points.default_guess: Continue independent branches and finish `failed` once every still-runnable branch has settled.

open_points.subject: business facts versus retained values
open_points.text: K-10 says “It stores no business fact” and also says it stores edge values and keeps “Values and the records that name them ... for as long as ... traces; this kernel expires nothing.”
open_points.question: Are business-valued run inputs and outputs retained indefinitely as trace-associated values, and what does “stores no business fact” exclude?
options: It retains copies but they are non-authoritative execution evidence
Business-valued payloads must be digested rather than stored
Only bounded non-business metadata may be retained
open_points.default_guess: Retain bounded copies as non-authoritative execution evidence and define “no business fact” as no authoritative business record.

open_points.subject: secret scanning of file responses
open_points.text: Secrets says an echoed credential is recognized and withheld, while K-10 says “the kernel does not inspect file content.”
open_points.question: Does verbatim secret detection apply to file bodies, and if so how can it be performed without inspecting file content?
options: Secret detection applies only to structured non-file values
Files are streamed through exact-byte secret detection without media inspection
Every service-returned file is withheld from agents
open_points.default_guess: Limit exact secret detection to structured non-file response values and rely on disclosure class for files.

open_points.subject: fixed MCP operation set
open_points.text: K-11 lists “inspect, author, try, run, resume, read traces, and the owner's approve, accept, activate, grant, revoke, resolve and cancel,” omitting explicit carriers for add trial, capture failure, release failed run, rollback, propose binding, compose/prove and refuse effect.
open_points.question: Which listed MCP operations carry every primary action, or must the fixed surface explicitly add operations for the omissions?
options: Define tagged subactions under inspect, author, try, approve and activate
Add one MCP operation per primary action
Use a single generic command operation with typed variants
open_points.default_guess: Keep a fixed surface but define explicit typed variants mapping every primary action to a named MCP operation.

open_points.subject: repair context and “recent” evidence
open_points.text: “For repair an agent receives one contract, its current implementation and that slot's recent traces and trial evidence” does not define the requesting action, selection of the slot, or what “recent” means.
open_points.question: Which action requests repair context, how is the slot selected, and what deterministic bound and ordering defines recent evidence?
options: A dedicated bounded repair-context request
An inspect query with explicit limit and cursor
The kernel automatically pushes context after every failure
open_points.default_guess: Provide an inspect repair-context variant with an explicit limit, newest-first ordering and cursor.

open_points.subject: function input disclosure ceilings
open_points.text: K-14 says proof checks delivery to “an input accepting less,” but only bindings declare “the highest class each input accepts”; no acceptance class is defined for function inputs or flow outputs.
open_points.question: What disclosure ceiling applies to every function input and flow output port, and where is it declared?
options: Every contract and flow port declares a ceiling
Function inputs always accept `personal_data`
A function input ceiling is inferred from its trial corpus
open_points.default_guess: Require every function and flow input/output port to declare its disclosure ceiling.

open_points.subject: classification of caller-supplied values
open_points.text: “Every value carries” a disclosure class, but the texts do not say who assigns or verifies the class of a flow's own input values.
open_points.question: Can an owner or agent label a supplied value, or is its class fixed by the input port or trusted provenance?
options: The flow input port fixes a minimum class and callers cannot downgrade it
The caller supplies the class
Flow inputs may come only from classified service outputs
open_points.default_guess: Have the flow input declaration fix the class or minimum class and forbid caller downgrades.

open_points.subject: photo-upload acceptance setup
open_points.text: “A flow takes an original invoice photo into custody through the owning service's declared operations” does not name the service operations, starting reference, terminal custody condition or expected run result.
open_points.question: What exact seeded service state, flow input, operations and observable service fact prove that the photo entered custody?
options: A fixture intake-record reference read from one service and written to a named custody operation
A caller-provided file upload
A source service streams the file to a destination service without a flow input
open_points.default_guess: Seed an intake record, pass its reference as a value, read its file through one operation and store it through a declared custody operation.

open_points.subject: required pending scenario
open_points.text: The photo case says it “shows ... `pending`” without saying whether the pending reason is an unreachable service or an unknown effect outcome, or how that state is induced reproducibly.
open_points.question: Which `pending` reason must the acceptance case demonstrate and what bounded fault injection creates it?
options: `outcome_unknown` after an ambiguous send
Service unreachable before a send
Both pending reasons in separate bounded cases
open_points.default_guess: Demonstrate both reasons with separate deterministic fault fixtures.

open_points.subject: third-party analysis acceptance oracle
open_points.text: “returns an analysis, releasing nothing” does not identify the third-party dataset, required functions, expected analysis, output schema or meaning of “releasing.”
open_points.question: What fixed input and expected output prove the analysis, and does “releasing nothing” mean no write effects, no external disclosure, or no files leaving the kernel?
options: A seeded dataset with exact expected structured analysis and only `read` operations
A human judgment of a free-text analysis
Any schema-valid output from agent-written functions
open_points.default_guess: Use a seeded dataset and exact structured expected result, with no non-read operation nodes or external disclosure.

open_points.subject: real service instances
open_points.text: “both cases pass against the real service instances” does not name the installation, fixture/reset procedure, required capabilities or whether disposable rigs count as real instances.
open_points.question: Which service instances run acceptance, how are they seeded and reset, and how is the test isolated from production effects?
options: Disposable real implementations selected by a dedicated acceptance installation
Production-like shared instances with cleanup
Mocks are permitted as real instances
open_points.default_guess: Use dedicated disposable instances of the real service implementations with deterministic seed and reset procedures.

open_points.subject: negative-case matrix
open_points.text: “each refusal of K-05 through K-09 is shown by a bounded negative case” does not enumerate whether this means one case per decision, one per stated refusal condition, or every possible failure branch.
open_points.question: Which exact K-05 through K-09 refusal and waiting conditions require individual negative cases and what observable result must each assert?
options: One case for every normative refusal condition stated in K-05 through K-09
One representative case per K decision
A later state supplies an explicit traceability matrix
open_points.default_guess: Require an explicit finite matrix with one case for every stated normative refusal condition and expected code, state and trace.

open_points.subject: Python function ABI
open_points.text: “Functions are written in Python only” does not settle the Python version, source/package form, entry point, value serialization or file-handle interface.
open_points.question: What exact Python ABI must every implementation conform to?
options: A single source file exposing a named function with JSON-compatible arguments
A zipped module with a manifest and named callable
Source read from standard input and result written to standard output
open_points.default_guess: Pin a Python version and require one source module exposing a fixed callable over kernel-defined typed values and file handles.

open_points.subject: standard-library availability
open_points.text: “the Python standard library only” does not say whether every standard-library module is available, including modules that open processes, sockets, native extensions or host resources forbidden by K-02.
open_points.question: Which standard-library modules or capabilities are allowed inside the sandbox?
options: An explicit allowlist compatible with the sandbox restrictions
All modules import, but prohibited operations fail at runtime
An explicit denylist for network, process, clock, randomness and host-access modules
open_points.default_guess: Publish a strict allowlist and reject imports outside it during admission.

open_points.subject: approval request equality
open_points.text: “Any difference at send ... asks again” defines multipart exceptions but not URL normalization, query ordering, header case and order, JSON serialization, transfer encoding or other transport framing.
open_points.question: What canonical representation is compared to decide whether the fully built request still matches the approval?
options: Compare a specified canonical semantic request representation
Compare serialized HTTP bytes except listed secret and framing fields
Compare method, normalized URL, selected headers and a body digest
open_points.default_guess: Compare method, normalized URL, canonical non-secret headers and a canonical body/parts digest, explicitly excluding transport framing.

open_points.subject: credential-change exception
open_points.text: “Any difference ... in headers ... asks again” is followed by “The credential's value is never shown, so rotating it voids nothing,” without defining which header fields are credential material or whether authentication scheme changes are also ignored.
open_points.question: Which request components are designated credentials and excluded from approval equality, and does a change of credential location or authentication scheme void approval?
options: Only configured secret values are ignored; header names and auth scheme remain covered
All authorization headers are excluded entirely
The manifest declares an approval-visible template and secret placeholders
open_points.default_guess: Have the pinned operation request template mark secret placeholders; ignore only their substituted values, while changes to names, locations or schemes void approval.
